reference.source: Textbook of Autoinflammation / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A recessive autoinflammatory disease caused by loss-of-function mutations in OTULIN, a deubiquitinating enzyme regulating linear ubiquitin chains
Presents in early infancy with recurrent fevers, painful nodular panniculitis, and failure to thrive
Neutrophilic panniculitis produces tender subcutaneous nodules and erythematous skin lesions
Additional features include diarrhoea, joint swelling, and marked systemic inflammation
Loss of OTULIN function dysregulates nuclear factor kappa B signalling, producing a pro-inflammatory state involving tumour necrosis factor
Anti-tumour necrosis factor therapy can be strikingly effective, and interleukin-1 blockade is also used
Early diagnosis and cytokine-directed treatment are important given the severity of infantile systemic inflammation
reference.pathophysiology: Otulipenia results from biallelic loss-of-function mutations in OTULIN, an enzyme that removes linear (methionine-1 linked) ubiquitin chains and thereby restrains the linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex and downstream nuclear factor kappa B signalling. Without functional OTULIN, linear ubiquitination accumulates and inflammatory signalling is inappropriately amplified, with increased production of tumour necrosis factor and other pro-inflammatory cytokines. This unrestrained signalling drives neutrophilic panniculitis, recurrent fevers, and multi-organ inflammation in infancy. The central role of tumour necrosis factor explains the marked response to anti-tumour necrosis factor therapy.
additionalDifferentials: Other panniculitis-associated autoinflammatory diseases such as CANDLE
additionalInvestigations: Acute-phase reactants, which are markedly raised
Full blood count and inflammatory markers to monitor systemic activity
Assessment of growth and gastrointestinal symptoms
redFlags: Severe systemic inflammation with haemodynamic instability in infancy
Profound failure to thrive despite treatment
Features suggesting evolving macrophage activation or multi-organ dysfunction
Extensive skin and soft-tissue inflammation with secondary infection
reference.prognosis: Otulipenia is a severe infantile-onset disease, but recognition and cytokine-directed therapy, particularly tumour necrosis factor blockade, can induce marked improvement and allow catch-up growth.
pitfalls: Mistaking neutrophilic panniculitis for infective cellulitis and delaying immunomodulation
Not distinguishing otulipenia from other panniculitis-associated autoinflammatory diseases
Overlooking the strong response to anti-tumour necrosis factor therapy
Delaying genetic testing in an infant with recurrent fevers and panniculitis
